1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4.strategy: Recaptures with the knight, which stands in the centre with open lines for all of White's pieces. White has fewer central pawns but more activity; the knights on d4 and c6 face each other, and neither side wants to trade first.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4.name: Sicilian Defence: Open

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6.strategy: The main line. The knight develops with a threat to the unprotected e4 pawn, so White has to deal with it, usually by developing the knight to c3, which also takes the c4 square away from White. Black keeps the pawn structure flexible.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 g6.strategy: Prepares ...Bg7, ...Nf6 and castling without spending a move on ...d6, so ...d5 stays available in one move. Black avoids the most dangerous direct attack, but accepts that White can clamp the centre with c4 and play a cramped, manoeuvring game.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 e5.strategy: Kicks the knight away at once and claims the centre. In return Black accepts a weak square on d5 and a backward d-pawn, while White's knight gets a forward post from which to attack the d6 square.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Qc7.strategy: Puts the queen on the c-file, where it supports the knight and prepares to meet the centre with ...e6 without committing the d-pawn. Solid and flexible, but it gives up the more active knight development and lets White build the centre as it wishes.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Qc7.name: Sicilian Defence: Flohr Variation

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Qb6.strategy: Attacks the knight a second time (the knight on c6 already hits it) and eyes the b2 pawn, so the natural defence with the bishop drops that pawn. White simply retreats the knight, and the queen has come out early without achieving much.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Qb6.name: Sicilian Defence: Godiva Variation

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 a6.strategy: Takes b5 away from White's knight and prepares queenside play, but does nothing for development and lets White clamp the centre. A slow, useful move rather than a challenge to the position.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 d5.strategy: Strikes at the centre before the pieces are out. White can steer into a queenless position, or take on d5 and chase the queen with developing moves, so Black's early break costs more than it gains.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 d5.name: Sicilian Defence: Nimzo-American Variation
